rows.title: Three weeks of silence, no shipping notice
rows.buyer_wants: The buyer wants to know why their order has not shipped or received tracking after 3 weeks.
reasoning: The buyer reports no shipping email or tracking number after 21 days.
Facts confirm has_tracking is false and tracking_uploaded_to_paypal is false.
The order was likely not shipped, so the buyer is correct that the item was not received.
The cheapest fair resolution is to fulfill the order immediately rather than refunding, as the buyer has not explicitly requested a refund.
guard_notes: No tracking on file, so delivery can't be proven; converted 'OFFER_REPLACEMENT' into a refund.

rows.title: Says nothing is at the door; carrier wrote the same address differently
rows.buyer_wants: The buyer wants to know why the package is missing despite tracking showing it was delivered.
reasoning: Tracking confirms delivery to the correct address on 2026-10-02.
The buyer has not explicitly requested a refund, only reported the item is missing.
The package is not marked as likely lost, and the buyer is within the return window.
Sharing tracking details is the appropriate first step to resolve the inquiry.

rows.title: Delivered a few doors down, two digits swapped in the carrier's scan
rows.buyer_wants: A replacement item shipped to them.
reasoning: Buyer explicitly asks for a replacement, not a refund.
Tracking shows 'DELIVERED' to the order address 5 days ago.
cannot_prove_delivery is false, so the merchant is not at fault for non-delivery.
Offering a replacement is the cheapest fair resolution that satisfies the buyer's request.

rows.title: Costly gadget barely works, buyer asks for a working one
rows.buyer_wants: A replacement for the defective fan.
reasoning: Buyer reports item is defective (grinding, dies after 10 mins) and asks for a working one.
Item is within the 30-day return window.
Store policy allows replacement or refund for items not as described.
Buyer explicitly requested a replacement ('working one') rather than a refund.
guard_notes: OFFER_REPLACEMENT is not possible on this dispute: PayPal does not allow it (allowed_response_options); proposing OFFER_RETURN_FOR_REFUND instead.

rows.title: Spoon cracked through and unusable, cheap item, buyer wants the money back
rows.buyer_wants: A full refund for the cracked spoon without returning the item.
reasoning: Buyer reports item arrived damaged (cracked).
Store policy states items under $20 that arrive damaged are refunded in full without return.
Fact 'refund_without_return_eligible' is true.
Buyer explicitly requested a refund, not a replacement.

rows.title: Assistant paid well over its owner's spending cap, nothing shipped yet
rows.buyer_wants: A refund because the AI assistant exceeded the $40 spending limit.
reasoning: The dispute is UNAUTHORISED, but facts show the purchase was made by the buyer's AI assistant (Nova).
The assistant followed the item instruction (olive, regular) but violated the spending limit ($64 > $40).
The buyer did not explicitly ask for a full refund in the message, only noting the price discrepancy.
Store policy allows for handling agent errors; a partial refund is a fair and cheap resolution to keep the sale.
cannot_prove_delivery is true, but the dispute is not 'not-received', so the specific refund rule for lost packages does not apply.

rows.title: Doesn't know the shop; the charge is a standing reorder by their assistant
rows.buyer_wants: A refund for an unauthorized charge they claim they did not make.
reasoning: The purchase was made by the buyer's AI assistant, Nova, which followed the specific instruction to reorder filters.
The $24.00 charge is within the assistant's $30.00 spending limit, so the transaction is valid.
Tracking confirms the item was delivered to the correct address, refuting the 'unauthorized' claim.
The merchant is not at fault as the assistant acted within its programmed parameters.

rows.title: Two identical charges, but the extra one was refunded yesterday
rows.buyer_wants: A refund for the duplicate charge on their order.
reasoning: Facts confirm duplicate_charge_found is true with 2 matching charges same day.
Facts show refund_issued is true with refunded_amount matching the dispute amount.
SUBMIT_REFUND_PROOF is the correct resolution to close the dispute with existing proof.
Buyer's request for a refund has already been satisfied by the system.

rows.title: Returned a mat, says no credit; the refund went out a week ago
rows.buyer_wants: Confirmation that the refund for the returned item has been processed.
reasoning: The buyer reports that the refund for a returned item has not been received.
Facts confirm the return was received and a full refund of $48.00 was already issued.
The dispute reason 'CREDIT_NOT_PROCESSED' is resolved by providing proof of the existing refund.
Submitting proof of the refund is the most direct and fair resolution.

rows.title: Return was delivered to the shop and nothing has been refunded
rows.buyer_wants: A refund for the returned jacket.
reasoning: The buyer returned the item and the return was received.
The buyer is requesting a refund.
The return was outside the 30-day window, but the item is already back.
Refunding is the cheapest fair resolution to close the dispute.
